methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Endurance Energy is a SPAC-stage climate and energy company founded by Andrew Redd that has raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine firms in the Climate & Energy sector: one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this analysis. The Climate & Energy sector contains eight same-sector comparables, but none satisfy the filtering criteria required for a defensible median calculation. Zero companies matched on stage, zero on adjacent stage, and zero fell within a similar valuation tier. A cross-sector median would introduce material noise given the heterogeneity of business models, capital intensity, and technology maturity within climate tech. Consequently, this traditional triangulation approach cannot be reliably deployed with the available dataset.

The sparse peer set and stage-specific scarcity of directly comparable data points represent the primary valuation constraint. Without sufficient narrow-band comparables, any quantitative range derived from median multiples would lack empirical support. Further data collection—particularly around SPAC-stage or Series C-equivalent valuations within frontier energy—would be necessary to establish a credible triangulated range. Current uncertainty is elevated given the absence of methodologically sound quantitative anchors.
